summary: The "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map" (Pegasus Martian Map) is an interactive 3D navigation and surface-mapping web application developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Utilizing official NASA and USGS planetary datasets, our tool provides immersive exploration of Martian locations, advanced scientific analysis layers, and real-time EVA (Extravehicular Activity) rover movement simulations. This project addresses planetary exploration challenges by delivering an accessible, data-driven survival and mission-planning interface for future space missions.
details:
Pegasus Martian Map is a 3D Martian navigation and Extravehicular Activity (EVA) planning platform built primarily with TypeScript (80%) and CesiumJS, powered by official NASA and USGS planetary datasets.

  • Features & Functionality: Users can explore high-priority sites like Mount Sharp and Jezero Crater, toggle real-time topographic and scientific analysis overlays, monitor telemetry, and run live EVA rover traversal simulations directly in the browser.
  • Impact: It transforms raw planetary science data into an intuitive, mission-control interface that improves spatial awareness, hazard evaluation, and route safety for future Mars exploration.
  • Tech Stack: TypeScript (80%), CesiumJS, HTML5/CSS, NASA/USGS planetary data, deployed on Vercel (pegasus-martian-map.vercel.app) with source code on GitHub.
